description: Changes #3, #4, #5, #6, #7, #8 (frontend/UI + supporting backend data): Make AI usage visible and honest in the UI, separate the deterministic decision engine from the AI explanation, strengthen the revenue-recovery story on the dashboard and customer detail, add runtime mode indicators (Payment mode, AI mode, Model) reflecting ACTUAL state, improve demo scenario clarity so the false-positive contrast is obvious, and verify/keep the human blacklist review boundary. Presentation and data-surfacing only; do NOT change engine/financial/risk/decision logic or thresholds, and do NOT fabricate numbers (use existing persisted/demo data or deterministic calculations already available).
steps: Depends on FEAT-002 (health/explain now expose actual source+model; ExplainResponse has model+fallbackReason; HealthResponse exists).

Change #6 mode indicators: On the Dashboard (web/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx), add a compact, non-misleading status strip that reflects ACTUAL runtime state by calling api.getHealth(): 'Payment mode: SIMULATION' (from paymentMode), 'AI mode: OPENROUTER' or 'AI mode: DETERMINISTIC FALLBACK' (from aiMode/llm), and 'Model: <configured model>'. Do not claim live Razorpay when in simulation. Style it subtly (e.g. a small badge row); reuse components/Badge.tsx and styles.css. Add minimal CSS as needed.

Change #3 + AI transparency in CustomerDetail (web/src/pages/CustomerDetail.tsx): Restructure the explanation area so the DECISION ENGINE section (risk score, band, behavioural evidence, final decision) is clearly separated from the AI EXPLANATION section. The AI section must show: provider/source (OpenRouter vs Deterministic fallback), the model used (explain.model), the generated explanation/message text, and, when explain.source==='deterministic' with a fallbackReason, a clear 'AI source: Deterministic fallback — Reason: <fallbackReason>' note. When source==='openrouter' show 'AI source: OpenRouter · Model: <model>'. Never imply the LLM made the suspension/decision — keep wording that the engine decides and the AI only phrases the explanation.

Change #4 revenue-recovery story on CustomerDetail: For a RECOVER customer, make WHY recovery is recommended and WHICH intervention obvious, e.g. a prominent 'RECOVER — Recommended action: <titleized recommendedAction> · Potential revenue recovered: <formatMoney(subscription.amount)>' block. Use existing data: decision outcome, recommendedAction, expectedRecoveryOutcome, subscription.amount/currency. For RESTRICT/SUSPEND, clearly label the framing as 'Revenue leakage prevention / access restriction' vs a 'Revenue recovery decision', distinguishing the two. Do not fabricate amounts; derive potential-recovered from the subscription amount that is at stake.

Change #5 dashboard storytelling on Dashboard.tsx: Reorder/relabel so the first view answers recovered / at-risk / pending / lost / who-needs-attention / why. Prioritize the metric hierarchy: Revenue Recovered, Revenue at Risk, Recovery Rate, Pending Recovery (bring these to the top). Make the 'Highest-priority customers' table clearly actionable: include the recommended action and/or outcome and a short 'why' (e.g. outcome + risk band) and keep the row click-through to the customer. Do not add unnecessary charts; refine existing labels/hierarchy only. All numbers come from the existing /api/dashboard revenue summary.

If the highest-priority table needs the recommended action / a short reason to be actionable, surface those fields: they are available via the dashboard revenue summary's highestPriorityCustomers (customerId, outcome, riskScore, amount). If a recommended action per priority customer is desired and not already present, add it to the revenue engine's HighPriorityCustomer output ONLY as pass-through of the existing decision's recommendedAction (no logic/threshold change) and thread it through app.ts toRevenueView/dashboard and web types. Keep this minimal and do not alter ranking math.

Change #7 demo scenario clarity: Improve labeling so a judge instantly sees the false-positive contrast, especially scenario 7 (genuine repeated failures -> RECOVER, NOT blacklist) vs scenario 6 (value extraction -> SUSPEND + blacklist recommended). This is presentation only: e.g. on CustomerDetail show a concise contextual tag/summary line for the decision (reuse the existing evidence and the seed scenario summary is NOT available to the API, so derive the framing from outcome + blacklistRecommended + pattern-over-band note already present). Ensure the 'Not blacklisted' vs 'Blacklist recommended (human review)' badges remain prominent. Do NOT change any scenario's intended outcome.

Change #8 human blacklist review boundary: Verify (do not weaken) that the engine only RECOMMENDS blacklist and merchant approve/reject/reinstate/restore controls work and write audit. The existing CustomerDetail review controls and app.ts /review already implement this. Confirm the UI copy makes clear blacklist is a recommendation requiring merchant approval and is never auto-applied. Keep the existing e2e coverage green; optionally add a focused assertion if useful.
Update web/src/api/types.ts and any component props for any new pass-through fields (e.g. highestPriorityCustomer.recommendedAction). Keep names matching backend JSON exactly.
Run `npm run build` (both workspaces) and confirm zero TypeScript/vite errors. Run `npm test` to confirm backend tests still pass (including any dashboard/revenue data-consistency assertions).
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows a runtime status strip with Payment mode (SIMULATION), AI mode (OPENROUTER or DETERMINISTIC FALLBACK), and Model, reflecting actual /api/health state.

CustomerDetail clearly separates the Decision engine section (risk, evidence, decision) from the AI explanation section (source, model, generated text, fallback status), and never implies the LLM made the decision.
When explanation used deterministic fallback, the UI shows 'Deterministic fallback' with the reason; when OpenRouter was used, it shows OpenRouter + the model.
A RECOVER customer clearly shows why recovery is recommended, the recommended intervention, and the potential recovered amount, using existing data.
Dashboard first view prioritizes Revenue Recovered, Revenue at Risk, Recovery Rate, Pending Recovery, and an actionable highest-priority customer table with outcome/why.
All 7 scenarios keep their intended outcomes; the scenario-6-vs-7 contrast is visually obvious; blacklist remains a merchant-approved recommendation with working review controls and audit.
web build is zero-error and backend tests remain green; no fabricated numbers.
verification: Run `npm run build` and confirm both server and web build with zero errors.
Run `npm test` from repo root and confirm all tests pass.
Start `npm run dev:server` backgrounded and curl `http://localhost:4000/api/health`, confirming it returns paymentMode simulation, the llm/ai mode, and the model; then stop the server.
findings: Implemented UI/presentation refinements (#3,#4,#5,#6 frontend,#7) and verified #8. Changes: (1) Dashboard.tsx — added ModeStrip via api.getHealth() showing Payment mode (SIMULATION), AI mode (OPENROUTER/DETERMINISTIC FALLBACK) and Model; reordered metrics into a recovery-first hierarchy (Revenue recovered, Revenue at risk, Recovery rate, Pending recovery) with a secondary row (Lost revenue, Total); promoted Highest-priority customers to a prominent full-width actionable table with Recommended action + a derived 'Why prioritized' column + revenue at stake, keeping row click-through. (2) CustomerDetail.tsx — added a revenue-framing block distinguishing 'Revenue recovery decision' (RECOVER/INTERVENE, shows recommended action + potential revenue recovered from subscription.amount) vs 'Revenue leakage prevention / access restriction' (RESTRICT/SUSPEND); relabeled evidence card as 'Decision engine — behavioural evidence' (deterministic) and reworked the explain section into 'AI explanation' that honestly shows OpenRouter+model vs Deterministic fallback+fallbackReason, with copy stating the engine decides and AI only phrases it. (3) styles.css — added minimal styles (mode-strip, recovery-frame, explain-source, ai-explanation/decision-engine accents, metric-grid-secondary) reusing existing tone vars. Backend pass-through: added optional recommendedAction to HighPriorityCustomer in revenue.ts (pure pass-through of the stored decision's recommendedAction via existing toRevenueView; NO ranking/threshold/financial change) and mirrored it in web types.ts; added a revenue.test.ts assertion verifying the pass-through and that ranking is unchanged. #7: scenario contrast surfaced via existing pattern-over-band note + prominent 'Not blacklisted' vs 'Blacklist recommended (human review)' badges + recovery framing copy ('repeated failure does not automatically mean abuse'); no scenario outcomes changed. #8: blacklist boundary unchanged — engine only recommends, merchant approve/reject/reinstate/restore controls + audit intact, no auto-apply. VERIFICATION: `npm run build` zero-error (server tsc + web tsc/vite). `npm test` 146/146 passing (145 baseline + 1 new revenue assertion); openrouter fallback console.warn and api.e2e 'payment.definitely_not_real' stderr are expected negative-path output. `curl /api/health` returned {status:ok,paymentMode:simulation,llm:openrouter,model:openai/gpt-4o-mini,aiMode:openrouter}; dashboard priority rows correctly carry recommendedAction where a stored action exists. No API key exposed anywhere. Did NOT commit/push per delegation instructions (a later step commits).
